title: source (src)
content:
Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

Parameters:
- getSource:

title: n
content:
Selects the given index:

for samples, it picks the sample by index, with wrap around
for scales, it picks the scale degree
for voicings, it picks the voice index

Parameters:
- value: sample index starting from 0

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*6").n("<0 1>")
```

title: i
content:
Selects the given degree. Currently used in xen and tune:

Parameters:
- value: 

```
i("0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7").xen("<5edo 10edo 15edo hexany15>")
```

title: note
content:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

a letter (a-g or A-G)
optional accidentals (b or #)
optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: c, bb, Bb, f#, c3, A4, Eb2, c#5
You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

```
note("c a f e")
```
```
note("c4 a4 f4 e4")
```
```
note("60 69 65 64")
```
```
note("fbb1 a#0 cbbb-1 e##-2").sound("saw")
```

title: accelerate
content:
A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

Parameters:
- amount: acceleration.

```
s("sax").accelerate("<0 1 2 4 8 16>").slow(2).osc()
```

title: velocity (vel)
content:
Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

```
s("hh*8")
.gain(".4!2 1 .4!2 1 .4 1")
.velocity(".4 1")
```

title: gain
content:
Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

Parameters:
- amount: gain.

```
s("hh*8").gain(".4!2 1 .4!2 1 .4 1").fast(2)
```

title: postgain
content:
Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8")
.compressor("-20:20:10:.002:.02").postgain(1.5)
```

title: amp
content:
Like gain, but linear.

Parameters:
- amount: gain.

```
s("bd*8").amp(".1*2 .5 .1*2 .5 .1 .5").osc()
```

title: fmh
content:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio.
Controls the timbre of the sound.
Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural,
while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.
A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmh2)

Parameters:
- harmonicity: 

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()
```

title: fmi (fm)
content:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.
A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into
each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into
fm3

Parameters:
- brightness: modulation index

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()
```
```
s("sine").note("F1").seg(8)
 .fm(4).fm2(rand.mul(4)).fm3(saw.mul(8).slow(8))
 .fmh(1.06).fmh2(10).fmh3(0.1)
```

title: fmenv (fme)
content:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..
A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmenv4)

Parameters:
- type: lin | exp

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()
```

title: fmattack (fmatt)
content:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation
A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)

Parameters:
- time: attack time

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()
```

title: fmwave
content:
Waveform of the fm modulator
A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmwave6)

Parameters:
- wave: waveform

```
n("0 1 2 3".fast(4)).scale("d:minor").s("sine").fmwave("<sine square sawtooth crackle>").fm(4).fmh(2.01)
```
```
n("0 1 2 3".fast(4)).chord("<Dm Am F G>").voicing().s("sawtooth").fmwave("brown").fm(.6)
```

title: fmdecay (fmdec)
content:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.
A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)

Parameters:
- time: decay time

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()
```

title: fmsustain (fmsus)
content:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase
A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)

Parameters:
- level: sustain level

```
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()
```

title: fmrelease (fmrel)
content:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released
A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

Parameters:
- time: release time

title: bank
content:
Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with s. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of s.

Parameters:
- bank: the name of the bank

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")
```

title: chorus
content:
mix control for the chorus effect

Parameters:
- chorus: mix amount between 0 and 1

```
note("d d a# a").s("sawtooth").chorus(.5)
```

title: attack (att)
content:
Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

Parameters:
- attack: time in seconds.

```
note("c3 e3 f3 g3").attack("<0 .1 .5>")
```

title: decay (dec)
content:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

Parameters:
- time: decay time in seconds

```
note("c3 e3 f3 g3").decay("<.1 .2 .3 .4>").sustain(0)
```

title: sustain (sus)
content:
Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

Parameters:
- gain: sustain level between 0 and 1

```
note("c3 e3 f3 g3").decay(.2).sustain("<0 .1 .4 .6 1>")
```

title: release (rel)
content:
Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

Parameters:
- time: release time in seconds

```
note("c3 e3 g3 c4").release("<0 .1 .4 .6 1>/2")
```

title: bpf (bandf, bp)
content:
Sets the center frequency of the band-pass filter. When using mininotation, you
can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

Parameters:
- frequency: center frequency

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*6").bpf("<1000 2000 4000 8000>")
```

title: bpq (bandq)
content:
Sets the band-pass q-factor (resonance).

Parameters:
- q: q factor

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bpf(500).bpq("<0 1 2 3>")
```

title: begin
content:
A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. 0.25 to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

Parameters:
- amount: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

```
samples({ rave: 'rave/AREUREADY.wav' }, 'github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')
s("rave").begin("<0 .25 .5 .75>").fast(2)
```

title: end
content:
The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

Parameters:
- length: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

```
s("bd*2,oh*4").end("<.1 .2 .5 1>").fast(2)
```

title: loop
content:
Loops the sample.
Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo.
To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

Parameters:
- on: If 1, the sample is looped

```
s("casio").loop(1)
```

title: loopBegin (loopb)
content:
Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and before loopEnd!
Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

Parameters:
- time: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

```
s("space").loop(1)
.loopBegin("<0 .125 .25>")._scope()
```

title: loopEnd (loope)
content:
End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and after loopBegin!

Parameters:
- time: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

```
s("space").loop(1)
.loopEnd("<1 .75 .5 .25>")._scope()
```

title: crush
content:
Bit crusher effect.

Parameters:
- depth: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

```
s("<bd sd>,hh*3").fast(2).crush("<16 8 7 6 5 4 3 2>")
```

title: coarse
content:
Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

Parameters:
- factor: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").coarse("<1 4 8 16 32>")
```

title: tremolo (trem)
content:
Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

Parameters:
- speed: modulation speed in HZ

```
note("d d d# d".fast(4)).s("supersaw").tremolo("<3 2 100> ").tremoloskew("<.5>")
```

title: tremolosync (tremsync)
content:
Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

Parameters:
- cycles: modulation speed in cycles

```
note("d d d# d".fast(4)).s("supersaw").tremolosync("4").tremoloskew("<1 .5 0>")
```

title: tremolodepth (tremdepth)
content:
Depth of amplitude modulation

Parameters:
- depth: 

```
note("a1 a1 a#1 a1".fast(4)).s("pulse").tremsync(4).tremolodepth("<1 2 .7>")
```

title: tremoloskew (tremskew)
content:
Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

Parameters:
- amount: between 0 & 1, the shape of the waveform

```
note("{f a c e}%16").s("sawtooth").tremsync(4).tremoloskew("<.5 0 1>")
```

title: tremolophase (tremphase)
content:
Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

Parameters:
- offset: the offset in cycles of the modulation

```
note("{f a c e}%16").s("sawtooth").tremsync(4).tremolophase("<0 .25 .66>")
```

title: tremoloshape (tremshape)
content:
Shape of amplitude modulation

Parameters:
- shape: tri | square | sine | saw | ramp

```
note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")
```

title: drive
content:
Filter overdrive for supported filter types

Parameters:
- amount: 

```
note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")
```

title: duckorbit (duck)
content:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.
Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

Parameters:
- orbit: target orbit

```
$: n(run(16)).scale("c:minor:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2)
$: s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit(2).duckattack(0.2).duckdepth(1)
```
```
$: n(run(16)).scale("c:minor:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2)
$: s("hh*16").orbit(3)
$: s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit("2:3").duckattack(0.2).duckdepth(1)
```

title: duckdepth
content:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

Parameters:
- depth: depth of modulation from 0 to 1

```
stack( n(run(8)).scale("c:minor").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2), s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit(2).duckattack(0.2).duckdepth("<1 .9 .6 0>"))
```
```
$: n(run(16)).scale("c:minor:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2)
$: s("hh*16").orbit(3)
$: s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit("2:3").duckattack(0.2).duckdepth("1:0.5")
```

title: duckonset (duckons)
content:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

Parameters:
- time: The onset time in seconds

```
// Clicks
sound: freq("63.2388").s("sine").orbit(2).gain(4)
duckerWithClick: s("bd*4").duckorbit(2).duckattack(0.3).duckonset(0).postgain(0)
```
```
// No clicks
sound: freq("63.2388").s("sine").orbit(2).gain(4)
duckerWithoutClick: s("bd*4").duckorbit(2).duckattack(0.3).duckonset(0.01).postgain(0)
```
```
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)
```

title: duckattack (duckatt, datt)
content:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

Parameters:
- time: The attack time in seconds

```
sound: n(run(8)).scale("c:minor").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2)
ducker: s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit(2).duckattack("<0.2 0 0.4>").duckdepth(1)
```
```
moreduck: n(run(8)).scale("c:minor").s("sawtooth").delay(.7).orbit(2)
lessduck: s("hh*16").orbit(5)
ducker: s("bd:4!4").beat("0,4,8,11,14",16).duckorbit("2:5").duckattack("0.4:0.1")
```

title: byteBeatExpression (bbexpr, bb)
content:
Create byte beats with custom expressions

Parameters:
- byteBeatExpression: bitwise expression for creating bytebeat

```
s("bytebeat").bbexpr('t*(t>>15^t>>66)')
```

title: byteBeatStartTime (bbst)
content:
Create byte beats with custom expressions

Parameters:
- byteBeatStartTime: in samples (t)

```
note("c3!8".add("{0 0 12 0 7 5 3}%8")).s("bytebeat:5").bbst("<3 1>".mul(10000))._scope()
```

title: channels (ch)
content:
Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

Parameters:
- channels: pattern the output channels

```
note("e a d b g").channels("3:4")
```

title: pw
content:
Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

Parameters:
- pulsewidth: 

```
note("{f a c e}%16").s("pulse").pw(".8:1:.2")
```
```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("pulse").pw("0 .75 .5 1")
```

title: pwrate (pwr)
content:
Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

Parameters:
- rate: 

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("pulse").pw("0.5").pwrate("<5 .1 25>").pwsweep("<0.3 .8>")
```

title: pwsweep (pws)
content:
Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

Parameters:
- sweep: 

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("pulse").pw("0.5").pwrate("<5 .1 25>").pwsweep("<0.3 .8>")
```

title: phaser (ph)
content:
Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

Parameters:
- speed: speed of modulation

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").release(0.5)
.phaser("<1 2 4 8>")
```

title: phasersweep (phs)
content:
The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

Parameters:
- phasersweep: most useful values are between 0 and 4000

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").release(0.5)
.phaser(2).phasersweep("<800 2000 4000>")
```

title: phasercenter (phc)
content:
The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

Parameters:
- centerfrequency: in HZ

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").release(0.5)
.phaser(2).phasercenter("<800 2000 4000>")
```

title: phaserdepth (phd, phasdp)
content:
The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

Parameters:
- depth: number between 0 and 1

```
n(run(8)).scale("D:pentatonic").s("sawtooth").release(0.5)
.phaser(2).phaserdepth("<0 .5 .75 1>")
```

title: channel
content:
Choose the channel the pattern is sent to

Parameters:
- channel: channel number

title: cut
content:
In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

Parameters:
- group: cut group number

```
s("[oh hh]*4").cut(1)
```

title: lpf (cutoff, ctf, lp)
content:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

Parameters:
- frequency: audible between 0 and 20000

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*6").lpf("<4000 2000 1000 500 200 100>")
```
```
s("bd*16").lpf("1000:0 1000:10 1000:20 1000:30")
```

title: lpenv (lpe)
content:
Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

Parameters:
- modulation: depth of the lowpass filter envelope between 0 and n

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(300)
.lpa(.5)
.lpenv("<4 2 1 0 -1 -2 -4>/4")
```

title: hpenv (hpe)
content:
Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

Parameters:
- modulation: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.hpf(500)
.hpa(.5)
.hpenv("<4 2 1 0 -1 -2 -4>/4")
```

title: bpenv (bpe)
content:
Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

Parameters:
- modulation: depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and n

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.bpf(500)
.bpa(.5)
.bpenv("<4 2 1 0 -1 -2 -4>/4")
```

title: lpattack (lpa)
content:
Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- attack: time of the filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(300)
.lpa("<.5 .25 .1 .01>/4")
.lpenv(4)
```

title: hpattack (hpa)
content:
Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- attack: time of the highpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.hpf(500)
.hpa("<.5 .25 .1 .01>/4")
.hpenv(4)
```

title: bpattack (bpa)
content:
Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- attack: time of the bandpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.bpf(500)

```

title: lpdecay (lpd)
content:
Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- decay: time of the filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(300)
.lpd("<.5 .25 .1 0>/4")
.lpenv(4)
```

title: hpdecay (hpd)

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")

.hpenv(4)
```

title: bpdecay (bpd)
content:

Parameters:
- decay: time of the bandpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.bpf(500)
.bpd("<.5 .25 .1 0>/4")
.bps(0.2)
.bpenv(4)
```

title: lpsustain (lps)
content:
Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- sustain: amplitude of the lowpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(300)
.lpd(.5)
.lps("<0 .25 .5 1>/4")
.lpenv(4)
```

title: hpsustain (hps)
content:
Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- sustain: amplitude of the highpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.hpf(500)
.hpd(.5)
.hps("<0 .25 .5 1>/4")
.hpenv(4)
```

title: bpsustain (bps)
content:
Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- sustain: amplitude of the bandpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.bpf(500)
.bpd(.5)
.bps("<0 .25 .5 1>/4")
.bpenv(4)
```

title: lprelease (lpr)
content:
Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- release: time of the filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.clip(.5)
.lpf(300)
.lpenv(4)
.lpr("<.5 .25 .1 0>/4")
```

title: hprelease (hpr)
content:
Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

Parameters:
- release: time of the highpass filter envelope

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")
.sound('sawtooth')
.clip(.5)
.hpf(500)
.hpenv(4)
.hpr("<.5 .25 .1 0>/4")
.release(.5)
```

```
note("c2 e2 f2 g2")

.clip(.5)

.bpenv(4)
```

title: ftype
content:
Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.

Parameters:
- type: 12db (0), ladder (1), or 24db (2)

```
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)
```
```
note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")
```

title: fanchor
content:
controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative

Parameters:
- center: 0 to 1

```
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")
```

title: hpf (hp, hcutoff)
content:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

Parameters:

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").hpf("<4000 2000 1000 500 200 100>")
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").hpf("<2000 2000:25>")
```

title: lprate
content:
Rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

```
note("<c c c# c c c4>*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(600).lprate("<4 8 2 1>")
```

title: lpsync
content:

- rate: rate in cycles

```
note("<c c c# c c c4>*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(600).lpsync("<4 8 2 1>")
```

title: lpdepth
content:
Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter

Parameters:
- depth: depth of modulation

```
note("<c c c# c c c4>*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(600).lpdepth("<1 .5 1.8 0>")
```

title: lpdepthfrequency (lpdepthfreq)
content:
Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter, in HZ

Parameters:
- depth: depth of modulation

```
note("<c c c# c c c4>*16").s("sawtooth").lpf(600).lpdepthfrequency("<200 500 100 0>")
```

title: vib (vibrato, v)
content:
Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.

Parameters:
- frequency: of the vibrato in hertz

```
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>")
._scope()
```
```
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()
```

title: noise
content:
Adds pink noise to the mix

Parameters:
- wet: wet amount

```
sound("<white pink brown>/2")
```

title: vibmod (vmod)
content:
Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set

Parameters:
- depth: of vibrato (in semitones)

```
note("a e").vib(4)
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>")
._scope()
```
```
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()
```

title: hpq (hresonance)
content:
Controls the high-pass q-value.

Parameters:
- q: resonance factor between 0 and 50

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").hpf(2000).hpq("<0 10 20 30>")
```

title: lpq (resonance)
content:
Controls the low-pass q-value.

Parameters:
- q: resonance factor between 0 and 50

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").lpf(2000).lpq("<0 10 20 30>")
```

title: djf
content:
DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

Parameters:
- cutoff: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

```
n(irand(16).seg(8)).scale("d:phrygian").s("supersaw").djf("<.5 .3 .2 .75>")
```

title: delay
content:
Sets the level of the delay signal.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

Parameters:
- level: between 0 and 1

```
s("bd bd").delay("<0 .25 .5 1>")
```
```
s("bd bd").delay("0.65:0.25:0.9 0.65:0.125:0.7")
```

title: delayfeedback (delayfb, dfb)
content:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

Parameters:
- feedback: between 0 and 1

```
s("bd").delay(.25).delayfeedback("<.25 .5 .75 1>")
```

title: delayspeed (delayt, dt)
content:
Sets the time of the delay effect.

Parameters:
- delayspeed: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

```
note("d d a# a".fast(2)).s("sawtooth").delay(.8).delaytime(1/2).delayspeed("<2 .5 -1 -2>")
```

title: delaytime (delayt, dt)
content:
Sets the time of the delay effect in seconds.

Parameters:
- delay: in seconds

```
note("d d a# a".fast(2))
.s("sawtooth")
.delay(.8)
.delaytime(1/2)
.delayspeed("<2 .5 -1 -2>")
```

title: delaysync (delays, ds)
content:
Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

Parameters:
- cycles: delay length in cycles

```
s("bd bd").delay(.25).delaysync("<1 2 3 5>".div(8))
```

title: lock
content:
Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

Parameters:
- enable: When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.

```
s("sd").delay().lock(1).osc()
```

title: detune (det)
content:
Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators.

Parameters:
- amount: 

```
note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")
```

title: unison
content:
Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators.

Parameters:
- numvoices: 

```
note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")
```

title: spread
content:
Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators

Parameters:
- spread: between 0 and 1

```
note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")
```

title: dry
content:
Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

Parameters:
- dry: 0 = wet, 1 = dry

```
n("[0,3,7](3,8)").s("superpiano").room(.7).dry("<0 .5 .75 1>").osc()
```

title: fadeTime (fadeOutTime)
content:
Used when using begin/end or chop/striate and friends, to change the fade out time of the 'grain' envelope.

Parameters:
- time: between 0 and 1

```
s("oh*4").end(.1).fadeTime("<0 .2 .4 .8>").osc()
```

title: freq
content:
Set frequency of sound.

Parameters:
- frequency: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

```
freq("220 110 440 110").s("superzow").osc()
```
```
freq("110".mul.out(".5 1.5 .6 [2 3]")).s("superzow").osc()
```

title: pattack (patt)
content:
Attack time of pitch envelope.

Parameters:
- time: time in seconds

```
note("c eb g bb").pattack("0 .1 .25 .5").slow(2)
```

title: pdecay (pdec)
content:
Decay time of pitch envelope.

Parameters:
- time: time in seconds

```
note("<c eb g bb>").pdecay("<0 .1 .25 .5>")
```

title: prelease (prel)
content:
Release time of pitch envelope

Parameters:
- time: time in seconds

```
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")
```

title: penv
content:
Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope.
If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

Parameters:
- semitones: change in semitones

```
note("c")
.penv("<12 7 1 .5 0 -1 -7 -12>")
```

title: pcurve
content:
Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

Parameters:
- type: 0 = linear, 1 = exponential

```
note("g1*4")
.s("sine").pdec(.5)
.penv(32)
.pcurve("<0 1>")
```

title: panchor
content:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:

anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]
anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note]
If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

Parameters:
- anchor: anchor offset

```
note("c c4").penv(12).panchor("<0 .5 1 .5>")
```

title: leslie
content:
Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

Parameters:
- wet: between 0 and 1

```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie("<0 .4 .6 1>").osc()
```

title: lrate
content:
Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

Parameters:
- rate: 6.7 for fast, 0.7 for slow

```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie(1).lrate("<1 2 4 8>").osc()
```

title: lsize
content:
Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

Parameters:
- meters: somewhere between 0 and 1

```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie(1).lrate(2).lsize("<.1 .5 1>").osc()
```

title: label
content:
Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

Parameters:
- label: text to display

title: octave (oct)
content:
Sets the default octave of a synth.

Parameters:
- octave: octave number

```
n("0,4,7").scale("F:minor").s('supersaw').octave("<0 1 2 3>")
```

title: orbit (o)
content:
An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

Parameters:
- number: 

```
stack(
  s("hh*6").delay(.5).delaytime(.25).orbit(1),
  s("~ sd ~ sd").delay(.5).delaytime(.125).orbit(2)
)
```

title: bus
content:
A bus is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with..
s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear
effects like distortion to multiple signals)
otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

Parameters:
- number:

title: busgain (bgain)
content:
Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

Parameters:
- number:

title: pan
content:
Sets position in stereo.

Parameters:
- pan: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

```
s("[bd hh]*2").pan("<.5 1 .5 0>")
```
```
s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))
```

title: panspan
content:
Controls how much multichannel output is fanned out

Parameters:
- span: between -inf and inf, negative is backwards ordering

```
s("[bd hh]*2").pan("<.5 1 .5 0>").panspan("<0 .5 1>").osc()
```

title: pansplay
content:
Controls how much multichannel output is spread

Parameters:
- spread: between 0 and 1

```
s("[bd hh]*2").pan("<.5 1 .5 0>").pansplay("<0 .5 1>").osc()
```

title: chord
content:
The chord to voice

Parameters:
- symbols: chord symbols to voice e.g., C, Eb, Fm7, G7. The symbols can be defined via addVoicings

```
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()
```

title: dictionary
content:
Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided

Parameters:
- dictionaryName: which dictionary (having been defined with addVoicings) to use

```
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)
```

title: anchor
content:
The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

Parameters:
- anchorNote: the note to align the voicing or scale to

```
anchor("<c4 g4 c5 g5>").chord("C").voicing()
```
```
n("0 .. 7").anchor("<c4 g4 c5 g5>").scale("<C:major F:minor>")
```

title: offset
content:
Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position

Parameters:
- shift: the amount to shift the voicing up or down

```
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time
```

title: octaves
content:
How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1

Parameters:
- count: the number of octaves

```
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()
```

title: mode
content:
How the voicing is aligned to the anchor


below: top note <= anchor


duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded


above: bottom note >= anchor


root: bottom note is the lowest root of the chord >= anchor


oldabove : old (buggy) behavior of above, kept for legacy reason


oldroot : old (buggy) behavior of root, kept for legacy reason

Parameters:
- modeName: one of {below | above | duck | root | oldabove | oldroot}

```
mode("<below above duck root>").chord("C").voicing()
```

title: room
content:
Sets the level of reverb.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

Parameters:
- level: 

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room("<0 .2 .4 .6 .8 1>")
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room("<0.9:1 0.9:4>")
```

title: roomlp (rlp)
content:
Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
- frequency: between 0 and 20000hz

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000)
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000)
```

title: roomdim (rdim)
content:
Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
- frequency: between 0 and 20000hz

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000).rdim(8000)
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000).rdim(400)
```

title: roomfade (rfade)
content:
Reverb fade time (in seconds).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
- seconds: for the reverb to fade

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000).rfade(0.5)
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000).rfade(4)
```

title: iresponse (ir)
content:
Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

Parameters:
- sample: to use as an impulse response

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).ir("<shaker_large:0 shaker_large:2>")
```

title: irspeed
content:
Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

Parameters:
- speed: 

```
samples('github:switchangel/pad')
$: s("brk/2").fit().scrub(irand(16).div(16).seg(8)).ir("swpad:4").room(.2).irspeed("<2 1 .5>/2").irbegin(.5).roomsize(.5)
```

title: irbegin (ir)
content:
Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

Parameters:
- begin: between 0 and 1

```
samples('github:switchangel/pad')
$: s("brk/2").fit().scrub(irand(16).div(16).seg(8)).ir("swpad:4").room(.65).irspeed("-2").irbegin("<0 .5 .75>/2").roomsize(.6)
```

title: roomsize (rsize, sz, size)
content:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see room.
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
- size: between 0 and 10

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).rsize(1)
```
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).rsize(4)
```

title: shape
content:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.
Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve
second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

Parameters:
- distortion: between 0 and 1

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").shape("<0 .2 .4 .6 .8>")
```

title: distort (dist)
content:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

Parameters:
- distortion: amount of distortion to apply
- volume: linear postgain of the distortion
- type: type of distortion to apply

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").distort("<0 2 3 10:.5>")
```
```
note("d1!8").s("sine").penv(36).pdecay(.12).decay(.23).distort("8:.4")
```
```
s("bd:4*4").bank("tr808").distort("3:0.5:diode")
```

title: distortvol (distortion, distvol)
content:
Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

Parameters:
- volume: linear postgain of the distortion

```
s("bd*4").bank("tr909").distort(2).distortvol(0.8)
```

title: distorttype (disttype)
content:
Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.

Parameters:
- type: type of distortion to apply

```
s("bd*4").bank("tr909").distort(2).distorttype("<0 1 2>")
```
```
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")
```

title: compressor
content:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")
More info here

```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8")
.compressor("-20:20:10:.002:.02")
```

title: speed
content:
Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

Parameters:
- speed: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

```
s("bd*6").speed("1 2 4 1 -2 -4")
```
```
speed("1 1.5*2 [2 1.1]").s("piano").clip(1)
```

title: stretch
content:
Changes the pitch of the sample without changing its speed.
The frequencies are multiplied by (factor + 1) for positive numbers
and by max(factor / 4 + 1, 0) for negative numbers.
So tuning up by octaves can be done with 1, 3, 7, ...
and tuning down by octaves with -2, -3, -3.5...

Parameters:
- factor: between -4 and inf. Positive increases pitch, 0 does nothing, negative decreases the pitch.

```
s("gm_flute").stretch("<2 1 0 -2>")
```

title: unit
content:
Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed.

Parameters:
- unit: see description above

```

```

title: squiz
content:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:
"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

Parameters:
- squiz: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

```

```

title: lfo
content:
Configures an LFO. Can be called in sequence like pat.lfo(...).lfo(...) to set up multiple LFOs.
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. lfo({ c: "lpf" }))
If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the lfo call will be used
(e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).lfo() to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a sometimes. See example below.

Parameters:
- config: LFO configuration.
- config.control: Node to modulate. Aliases: c
- config.subControl: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
- config.rate: Modulation rate. Aliases: r
- config.sync: Tempo-synced modulation rate. Aliases: s
- config.depth: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
- config.depthabs: Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
- config.dcoffset: DC offset / bias for the waveform. Aliases: dc
- config.shape: Shape index. Aliases: sh
- config.skew: Skew amount. Aliases: sk
- config.curve: Exponential curve amount. Aliases: cu
- config.retrig: If > 0.5, the LFO will retrigger on each event. Aliases: rt
- config.fxi: FX index to target
- id: ID to use for this modulator

```
s("saw").note("F1").lpf(500).lfo()
```
```
s("saw").lfo().lpf(500).lfo({ s: 0.3 })
```
```
s("saw").lpf(500).diode(0.3)
  .lfo({ c: "lpf" })
```
```
s("pulse").lpf(500).lfo()
  .lfo({ c: "s" })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.lfo({ s: "8" }, 1)) // lfo #1 (0-indexed)
```
```
s("pulse").lpf(500).lfo({ depth: 4 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .lfo({ c: "s" })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.lfo({ s: "8" }, 'lpf_mod'))
```

title: env
content:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. env({ c: "lpf" }))
If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the env call will be used
(e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }) to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a sometimes. See example below.

Parameters:
- config: Envelope configuration.
- config.control: Node to modulate. Aliases: c
- config.subControl: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
- config.depth: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
- config.depthabs: Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
- config.attack: Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a
- config.decay: Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d
- config.sustain: Sustain depth. Aliases: sus, s
- config.release: Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r
- config.acurve: Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac
- config.dcurve: Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc
- config.rcurve: Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc
- config.fxi: FX index to target
- id: ID to use for this modulator

```
s("saw").note("F1").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
```
```
s("saw").env({ d: 1 }).note("F1")
  .lpq(4).lpf(50)
  .env({ a: 0.1, d: 1, ac: 0.8, dc: 0.3, depth: 50 })
```
```
s("saw").lpf(500).diode(0.3)
  .env({ c: "lpf", a: 0.5, d: 0.5 })
```
```
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)
```
```
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))
```

title: bmod
content:
Modulates with the output from a given bus.
Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators
Send to an audio bus with otherPat.bus(..).
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:

Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" }))
If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the bmod call will be used
(e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 }) to modulate lpf)

Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a sometimes. See example below.

Parameters:
- config: Bus modulation configuration.
- config.bus: Bus to get modulation signal from
- config.control: Node to modulate. Aliases: c
- config.subControl: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
- config.depth: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
- config.depthabs: Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
- config.dc: DC offset prior to application
- config.fxi: FX index to target
- id: ID to use for this modulator

```
modulator: s("one").seg(64).gain(slider(0, 0, 1)).bus(1).dry(0)
carrier: s("saw").bmod({ b: 1 })
```

title: transient
content:
Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients
and sustains

Parameters:
- attack: Emphasis on transients; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)
- sustain: Emphasis on the sustains; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)

```
s("bd").transient("<-1 -0.5 0 0.5 1>")
```
```
s("hh*16").bank("tr909").transient("<-1:1 1:-1>")
```

title: drawLine
content:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span.
Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up.
Character legend:

"|" cycle separator
"-" hold previous value
"." silence

Parameters:
- pattern: the pattern to use
- chars: max number of characters (approximately)

```
const line = drawLine("0 [1 2 3]", 10); // |0--123|0--123
console.log(line);
silence;
```

title: euclid
content:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.
A negative number of pulses inverts the pattern
so pulses happen in the gaps of the normal euclidean rhythm.
A negative number of steps changes it into euclidLegato.

Parameters:
- pulses: the number of onsets/beats
- steps: the number of steps to fill

```
// The Cuban tresillo pattern.
note("c3").euclid(3,8)
```

title: euclidRot
content:
Like euclid, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

Parameters:
- pulses: the number of onsets/beats
- steps: the number of steps to fill
- rotation: offset in steps

```
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)
```

title: euclidLegato
content:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.
A negative number of steps changes it into euclid.

Parameters:
- pulses: the number of onsets/beats
- steps: the number of steps to fill
- rotation: offset in steps
- pat: 

```
note("c3").euclidLegato(3,8)
```

title: euclidLegatoRot
content:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence.
A negative number of steps changes it into euclidRot.

Parameters:
- pulses: the number of onsets/beats
- steps: the number of steps to fill
- rotation: offset in steps

```
note("c3").euclidLegatoRot(3,5,2)
```

title: euclidish (eish)
content:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as
sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the
same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

Parameters:
- pulses: the number of onsets
- steps: the number of steps to fill
- groove: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

```
sound("hh").euclidish(7,12,sine.slow(8))
.pan(sine.slow(8))
```

title: clearScope
Pattern
content:
Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

Parameters:
- query: The function that maps a State to an array of Hap.

title: withValue (fmap)
content:
Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of
each hap. It has the alias fmap.

Parameters:
- func: to to apply to the value

```
"0 1 2".withValue(v => v + 10).log()
```

title: fmap
content: see withValue

title: appWhole
content:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to
resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that
pattern of functions.

Parameters:
- whole_func: 
- func:

title: appBoth
content:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps
with those in the given pattern of values.  A new pattern is returned, with
each matching value applied to the corresponding function.
In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps
are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the
intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

Parameters:
- pat_val:

title: appLeft
content:
As with appBoth, but the whole timespan is not the intersection,
but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called
on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets,
are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left
hand or inner pattern).

Parameters:
- pat_val:

title: appRight
content:
As with appLeft, but whole timespans are instead taken from the
pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer
pattern.

Parameters:
- pat_val:

title: queryArc
content:
Query haps inside the given time span.

Parameters:
- begin: from time
- end: to time

```
const pattern = sequence('a', ['b', 'c'])
const haps = pattern.queryArc(0, 1)
console.log(haps)
silence
```

title: splitQueries
content:
Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes
some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to
happen within a cycle.

title: withQuerySpan
content:
Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query
timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

Parameters:
- func: the function to apply

title: withQueryTime
content:
As with withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to both the
begin and end time of the query timespan.

Parameters:
- func: the function to apply

title: withHapSpan
content:
Similar to withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to the timespans
of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where
present, whole timespans).

Parameters:
- func:

title: withHapTime
content:
As with withHapSpan, but the function is applied to both the
begin and end time of the hap timespans.

Parameters:
- func: the function to apply

title: withHaps
withHap
setContext
content:
Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

Parameters:
- context:

title: withContext
content:
Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

Parameters:
- func:

title: stripContext
content: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

title: withLoc
content:
Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the
context of every hap.

Parameters:

- end: end offset

title: filterHaps
content:
Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

Parameters:
- hap_test: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

```
s("bd*8").velocity(rand).filterHaps((h) => (h.whole.begin % 1) < h.value.velocity)
```

title: filterValues
content:
As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values
inside haps.

Parameters:
- value_test: 

```
const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")
kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)
snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')
bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)
```

title: removeUndefineds
content:
Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from
query results.

title: onsetsOnly
content:
Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap
with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time
as its part timespan.

title: discreteOnly
content:
Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole'
timespans) removed from query results.

title: defragmentHaps
content:
Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole.  Only
intended for use in tests.

title: firstCycle
content:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when
debugging a pattern.

Parameters:
- with_context: set to true, otherwise the context field
will be stripped from the resulting haps.

title: firstCycleValues
content: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

title: showFirstCycle
content: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

title: sortHapsByPart
content:
Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly
of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

title: asNumber
content: Returns a new pattern with all values parsed as numerals.

title: layer
content:
Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

```
"<0 2 4 6 ~ 4 ~ 2 0!3 ~!5>*8"
  .layer(x=>x.add("0,2"))
  .scale('C minor').note()
```

title: superimpose
content:
Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

```
"<0 2 4 6 ~ 4 ~ 2 0!3 ~!5>*8"
  .superimpose(x=>x.add(2))
  .scale('C minor').note()
```

title: log
content:
Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

```
s("bd sd").log()
```

title: logValues
content:
A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters)
within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

```
s("bd sd").gain("0.25 0.5 1").n("2 1 0").logValues()
```

title: into
content:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern.
True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the
source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be
applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern
to be played unchanged.

```
sound("bd sd ht lt").into("1 0", hurry(2))
```

title: arpWith
content:
Selects indices in in stacked notes.

```
note("<[c,eb,g]!2 [c,f,ab] [d,f,ab]>")
.arpWith(haps => haps[2])
```

title: arp
content:
Selects indices in in stacked notes.

```
note("<[c,eb,g]!2 [c,f,ab] [d,f,ab]>")
.arp("0 [0,2] 1 [0,2]")
```

title: set
content:
When called on a pattern a, with a input pattern b (a.set(b)),
combines a and b such that anything defined in b
and anything defined in a that is not defined in b
will be in the resulting pattern.
The structure is maintained from a,
because the default pattern alignment is in,
see the section on Pattern Alignment
in the technical manual in the docs
This is the inverse of keep
See examples below

Parameters:
- pat: 

```
// because input pattern has `s` set,
// it overrides the "sine" declared earlier
note("c a f e").s("sine").set(s("triangle"))
```

title: keep
content:
When called on a pattern a, with a input pattern b (a.keep(b)),
combines a and b such that anything defined in a,
and anything defined in b that is not defined in a
will be in the resulting pattern
The structure is maintained from a,
because the default pattern alignment is in,
see the section on Pattern Alignment
in the technical manual in the docs
This is the inverse of set
See examples below

Parameters:
- pat: 

```
// notes, already defined, will stay "c a f e",
// while "s", not defined, will be set to "piano"
note("c a f e").keep(note("e f a c").s("piano"))
```

title: add
sub
content:
Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.

```
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.
```

title: mul

Multiplies each number by the given factor.

```
"<1 1.5 [1.66, <2 2.33>]>*4".mul(150).freq()
```

title: mod

title: brshift

title: lt

performs a < b

Parameters:
- a: 
- b:

title: gt
content:
performs a > b

Parameters:
- a: 
- b:

title: lte
